Scope

Twenty-six independent offline Standard scans contributed to this aggregate. Findings cover production runtime, deployment ingress, telemetry, verification scripts, native tests, and the host benchmark self-test. The newest scan corroborated JA4 enforcement ordering and triggering-slot closure, identified a distinct JA4 baseline classification issue, and corroborated stale DNS incident family state. This additional independent scan corroborated the JA4 offender-closure and late Block All write paths, and identified a distinct loss of JA4 triggering-peer attribution across domains. The newest scan adds a conditional plain-DNS resolver origin risk and corroborates three established findings. The assigned scan corroborated the JA4 offender-closure, boot fixture, and benchmark B8 temp-file paths. The assigned worker independently corroborated the shutdown E2E no-admission false-pass path.

Threat Model

Alumina is a Linux single-binary HTTP/1.1 CONNECT egress proxy. It reads CWD-relative config.toml, checks Linux privileges, initializes bounded DNS/cache/log/traffic storage, resolves configured allowlist names, binds a listener, and runs one owner loop for DNS refresh and client tunnels (src/main.rs:14-33,67-108; src/boot/mod.rs:83-98; src/runtime/storage.rs:349-373,1460-1496; src/runtime/owner.rs:1-9). Reference deployment uses a dedicated VM, host networking, an external VPC firewall and stdout collector; local QA may use loopback (docs/deployment.md:1-26,45-73,96-129; README.md:92-105). A later independent static scan identified a JA4 block-action bypass and deadline transition bypasses in the serving reactor; these are conditional on configured policy and precise timing, respectively. The latest scan also found a boot test fixture directory with a predictable path and nonexclusive child write, alongside previously identified truncating test log sinks. The newest review identified a distinct symlink traversal gap in the local unsafe-surface docs gate and a terminal logging priority issue that can displace shutdown_final under queue pressure. This scan confirmed a conditional listener retry delay after transient accept errors and a symlinked test-module bypass of the parentage gate. This follow-up also identified conditional 32-bit event-token generation truncation after repeated slot reuse; the published appliance targets x86_64. The latest independent review corroborated the JA4 block bypass and predictable test log path; both are accounted for in their established findings. The latest scan added a conditional subnet-wide reference ingress exposure and a missed early-activity telemetry path for combined upstream error/readiness events; actual deployment and event frequency remain unverified. The latest worker identified a separate false-pass path in the shutdown E2E no-admission witness: a reachable first post-signal connection can be forgotten if a second probe is refused; current proxy behavior was not reproduced. The newest worker also found a conditional shared pending-pool exhaustion path: incomplete CONNECT heads can occupy all 128 pending setups for up to ten seconds each and cause later clients to receive 503. The latest independent review found a distinct DNS incident reporting error: after full recovery, a later one-family incident can inherit the other family's earlier failure snapshot. The newest scan identifies a conditional DNS-derived destination redirection path when a bare-IP plain resolver and resolver_trusted assurance are used; actual operator configuration and on-path adversary position are unknown. The assigned worker corroborated the established JA4 offender-closure and shared-host boot and benchmark temp-file findings. The assigned reducer worker independently corroborated the shutdown E2E no-admission false-pass path.

Trust Boundaries

  • Host/operator to proxy boot: config.toml is opened once, bounded to 16 KiB and validated; preflight rejects root UIDs, nonempty capabilities or missing no_new_privs. Host owns file permissions and process privileges (src/main.rs:14-33; src/config/mod.rs:537-586; src/boot/preflight.rs:88-139).
  • Workload/client to listener: bounded CONNECT parsing and exact normalized hostname:port allowlist matching gate the upstream dial. Configured tripwire actions form a separate enforcement path (src/inspection/connect.rs:229-251,370-401; src/runtime/tunnel.rs:768-782,873-902; src/runtime/reactor.rs:2470-2522).
  • Resolver to cache: configured numeric addresses use TCP 53 for bare IP or DoT 853 for FQDN; pinned DoT checks SAN and SPKI, unpinned DoT with empty roots fails closed. Parsing and publication enforce bounds, query identity, generation and assurance; plain DNS has no authenticated-origin proof (src/dns/resolver.rs:190-230; src/dns/transport.rs:805-832,1674-1691,2424-2438; src/dns/publication.rs:98-135).
  • Proxy to upstream: current admissible cache binding and approved port yield numeric TCP peer; dial rechecks binding and TLS ClientHello must match SNI/profile before relay. Client authenticates upstream TLS (src/runtime/tunnel.rs:832-846,873-902; src/runtime/reactor.rs:2588-2634,2797-2854; src/runtime/gate.rs:7-23).
  • Proxy to stdout collector: bounded nonblocking queue and loss accounting end at fd 1; collection and alerts are host responsibilities (src/log/mod.rs:1-15; src/log/sink.rs:9-26,90-173; docs/monitoring.md:41-50).
  • Workload versus deployment confinement: separate runtime/network identities and VPC firewall prevent direct egress and workload-controlled restarts; proxy owns CONNECT policy, not host firewall or lifecycle (docs/deployment.md:3-43; src/enforcement/state.rs:218-249).
  • Local co-tenant to test runner (conditional): test-only helpers derive PID/counter paths under std::env::temp_dir() and open with create+truncate; a preplaced symlink can redirect truncation if host symlink policy permits. Production serving does not call them (src/log/tests.rs:21-35; src/runtime/storage/startup_integration.rs:585-600; src/log/mod.rs:1041-1042; src/runtime/storage.rs:1672-1675).
  • Client to listener: any reachable TCP peer may send plaintext CONNECT without client authentication; bounded framing and exact normalized hostname:port membership govern authorization; Proxy-Authorization is ignored (src/runtime/reactor.rs:1876-1937; src/inspection/connect.rs:229-327; src/runtime/tunnel.rs:768-782; docs/alumina-proxy.md:78-83).
  • Reachable clients supply plaintext HTTP/1.1 CONNECT; an 8 KiB parser, exact allowlist pair check, DNS evidence, setup deadline, attempt limit, and per-dial peer admission govern upstream TCP opening (src/inspection/connect.rs:184-251; src/config/mod.rs:246-255; src/runtime/tunnel.rs:768-903; src/runtime/reactor.rs:2626-2644). No client source authentication is shown at accept; documented appliance ingress firewall owns reachability (src/runtime/reactor.rs:1876-1905; docs/deployment.md:22-26).
  • TLS ClientHello is a second boundary: TLS 1.3 offer, exactly one matching SNI, no ECH, and a two-barrier gate before relay (src/inspection/client_hello.rs:700-715,862-886; src/runtime/gate.rs:1-23,193-228). The client verifies upstream certificate (README.md:48-50).
  • Configured numeric resolvers supply DNS over TCP/53 or DoT/853. Pinned DoT verifies FQDN/SAN and SPKI; unpinned DoT uses empty roots and fails closed. Reply parser checks transaction/question identity and CNAME bailiwick. Plain TCP DNS lacks cryptographic origin authentication (src/config/mod.rs:667-717; src/dns/resolver.rs:184-230; src/dns/transport.rs:801-832,3199-3214; src/dns/wire.rs:1217-1277,1438-1485).
  • Linux process preflight requires non-root UIDs, no capabilities, and no_new_privs; deployment example supplies these host controls (src/boot/preflight.rs:88-129; docs/deployment.md:96-120).
  • CONNECT/parser/allowlist/TLS/ECH controls differ from per-domain early-data and JA4; class-specific gates govern all-scope latching (src/config/mod.rs:720-760,983-989; src/enforcement/state.rs:264-345).
  • Operator and host control config, firewall, image, registry credentials, and stdout collection. In-memory block state is not a host firewall; same-pod sidecar does not provide documented isolation (docs/deployment.md:3-43; README.md:56-62).
  • Within an admitted tunnel, JA4 baseline overflow and connect/setup/idle deadlines are enforcement boundaries. JA4 verdicts need to precede upstream forwarding; deadline checks need to guard the state transition and timer replacement (src/runtime/reactor.rs:2415-2425,2851-2905,2651-2660,2939,2981-3006).
  • Local co-tenant to native test runner (conditional): predictable PID/counter temp paths are used by log and startup test sinks and a boot fixture directory. Nonexclusive opens or reuse of a planted directory and config.toml child can overwrite runner-writable files if shared temp access and host permissions allow it (src/log/tests.rs:21-35; src/runtime/storage/startup_integration.rs:585-600; tests/support/temp_dir.rs:8-24).
  • Contributor-controlled repository source to local docs verification: a resolving production .rs symlink may be admitted while the preferred ripgrep unsafe scan omits its path; gate assurance depends on a reviewer or workflow using that local result (scripts/verify.sh:859-979).
  • Client-driven event pressure to terminal stdout reporting: a reserved monitor summary can displace a normal shutdown_final record on a near-full bounded queue; process exit status remains separately observable (src/runtime/owner.rs:30-40; src/log/queue.rs:206-227).
  • Local co-tenant to host benchmark verifier (conditional): the documented host self-test defaults to /tmp and writes fixed output and TLS artifact paths; planted symlinks can redirect runner writes if shared temp access and host symlink policy permit (docs/benchmarks/e2micro-suite.md:184-190; scripts/bench_workload.py:2079-2097,2710-2715,3402-3403).
  • Local co-tenant to shutdown E2E runner (conditional): fixed /tmp/shutdown-{name}.log opens with wb may follow a planted symlink to a runner-writable target when the cases execute in a shared temporary namespace (scripts/e2e_shutdown.py:809-810,1252).
  • Client and OS accept pressure to listener availability: after transient accept error the reactor's retry deadline must wake polling and rearm queued clients (src/runtime/reactor.rs:1536,1900,3272).
  • Contributor-controlled module declarations and symlinked test leaves to the local docs gate: every admitted test-named path must have actual cfg(test) parentage before unsafe exemption (scripts/verify.sh:872,896,934).
  • Listener clients to slot readiness on a 32-bit build: per-slot u64 generations are packed into usize event tokens, whose 21-bit generation field can wrap before the stored counter (src/runtime/reactor.rs:1920-1933,3399-3406).
  • Local shutdown E2E harness to no-admission verdict: a post-SIGTERM reachable connect must remain a failing observation across subsequent samples; probe_refused_sampled currently substitutes a second probe (scripts/e2e_shutdown.py:147-190,226-239,1047,1204).
  • Reachable listener peers share one pending setup pool without per-peer quotas. A peer can hold slots with incomplete CONNECT heads until the ten-second setup deadline; availability impact requires another client sharing the listener (src/inspection/connect.rs:241-251; src/runtime/tunnel.rs:439-452).
  • Resolver failure and recovery outcomes to operator incident telemetry: a newly opened window should report only the current A/AAAA family snapshots; stale state from a closed window can misattribute a later incident (src/runtime/storage.rs:784-828; src/dns/incident_report.rs:98-109,321-342,467-481).

Attacker Capabilities

  • Compromised workload can issue arbitrary CONNECT and ClientHello bytes and attempt direct calls if deployment permits, but does not thereby own config, proxy, resolver or firewall (README.md:8-16; docs/deployment.md:3-36).
  • Untrusted DNS peer or compromised plain resolver can control replies; pinned DoT changes resolver-hop authentication, while DNSSEC root validation remains external (src/dns/resolver.rs:190-230; src/dns/transport.rs:805-832; README.md:51-55).
  • TCP peer reaching listener can consume bounded setup capacity and receive fixed refusal statuses; reachability is deployment controlled (src/runtime/tunnel.rs:43-57; src/runtime/reactor.rs:1876-1900).
  • Host operator can change image/config, collector, restart and firewall; this is preexisting authority (docs/deployment.md:45-73,96-113).
  • A local co-tenant may create entries in a shared writable temp directory, but cannot thereby control production proxy traffic or operator config; the test-file clobber additionally requires predictable placement, permitted symlink following, and a runner-writable target (src/log/tests.rs:21-35).
  • A compromised workload controls its CONNECT and ClientHello bytes and any direct network route left by deployment, but is not assumed to control config, host, resolver pin, or firewall (README.md:8-16; docs/deployment.md:3-7).
  • A listener-reachable party can send malformed or allowed-looking CONNECTs and consume bounded setup capacity; external reachability is unknown (src/runtime/reactor.rs:1876-1933; src/runtime/tunnel.rs:43-57).
  • A DNS/network adversary may influence plain TCP DNS, while pinned DoT and reply validation are separate controls; trusted config and declared recursive policy are not assumed compromised (src/dns/resolver.rs:184-230; src/dns/transport.rs:801-832; src/dns/wire.rs:1217-1277).

Security Objectives

  • Only exact configured FQDN:port may produce an upstream connection to an eligible current cache address before expiry (src/runtime/tunnel.rs:832-846,873-902; src/runtime/reactor.rs:2588-2634).
  • No tunnel bytes cross either direction until initial ClientHello passes TLS 1.3 profile, ECH and SNI checks; client verifies upstream certificate (src/runtime/gate.rs:7-23,114-127; src/inspection/client_hello.rs:874-886).
  • DNS publication preserves query identity/generation and per-entry assurance; strong modes require pins and declared external root-validating/no-stale resolver policy (src/config/mod.rs:631-643,667-690; src/dns/publication.rs:98-135; src/dns/cache.rs:925-947).
  • Tripwire block state and limits remain bounded and process-owned; deployment prevents direct egress and restart bypass (src/enforcement/state.rs:218-249; docs/deployment.md:3-43).
  • Logging cannot block the serving loop; operators collect stdout and detect loss (src/log/sink.rs:9-26,90-173; docs/monitoring.md:41-50).
  • Test sink files should be exclusively created in private or unpredictable temp locations so a lower-privilege local user cannot redirect truncation (src/runtime/owner/tests.rs:1116-1134).
  • Bind every dial to exact configured hostname:port and currently admissible DNS-derived eligible address with bounded attempts/deadlines (src/config/mod.rs:251-255; src/runtime/tunnel.rs:879-961; src/runtime/reactor.rs:2626-2644; src/eligibility.rs:38-83).
  • Prevent relay before validated ClientHello gate; preserve TLS 1.3, SNI and ECH policy (src/runtime/gate.rs:7-23; src/inspection/client_hello.rs:700-715,874-886).
  • Strong DNS assurance requires pinned resolvers and operator root-validating/no-stale declaration, not local DNSSEC validation (src/config/mod.rs:631-643,678-690; src/dns/cache.rs:516-528; README.md:64-89).
  • Maintain Linux privilege prerequisites, workload/appliance separation, bounded state, and rejection observability (src/boot/preflight.rs:88-112; docs/deployment.md:3-26; src/inventory.rs:10-49; docs/monitoring.md:3-9).
  • Configured JA4 Block Connection or Block Domain must stop the triggering tunnel before post-verdict upstream bytes; connect, setup, and idle deadlines must remain effective at their protected transitions.
  • Native test fixtures should claim private temporary files and directories exclusively and reject planted symlinks before writing config.toml or sink data.
  • Local unsafe-surface verification should account for all compiled production Rust through the admitted source paths, including symlinks.
  • When terminal records compete for bounded queue capacity, preserve the typed shutdown verdict according to an explicit priority policy.
  • Shutdown E2E case logs should be created inside a private, owned workspace with exclusive no-follow semantics.
  • Rearm the listener promptly when its bounded accept-error pause expires, even without unrelated readiness.
  • Listener accept backoff should enforce its 100 ms retry cadence and wake an otherwise quiet owner; live slot readiness must remain matchable after generation-field wrap on supported targets.
  • Associate each JA4 change fingerprint with its own triggering peer address in the per-domain monitor report.

Assumptions

  • No production deployment, operator config, firewall, resolver policy or collector configuration was supplied (README.md:92-101).
  • Reference appliance maps /config.toml with WORKDIR /, while local binary reads ./config.toml from its launch directory; there are no CLI/environment policy overrides (src/main.rs:14-17; docs/deployment.md:60-73,96-104).
  • Reference firewall permits upstream TCP 443 while proxy accepts configured ports 1..65535; non-443 entries need firewall change. This is a conditional availability mismatch (src/config/mod.rs:38-59,121-135; src/runtime/reactor.rs:2588-2607; docs/deployment.md:21-26).
  • Unpinned DoT has empty trust roots and fails closed; pinned DoT certificate validity outside the window is warning-only by documented design (src/dns/transport.rs:805-832; docs/trust-telemetry-design.md:87-89).
  • Proxy does not establish DNSSEC anchors or external resolver no-stale behavior; recursive_dnssec_policy is an operator declaration (src/config/mod.rs:631-643,667-690; README.md:64-73).
  • Reference host uses registry credential helper and DOCKER_CONFIG=/var/lib/docker/.docker; helper file permissions are outside inspected implementation (docs/deployment.md:96-104).
  • The reference QA harness stages /work/config.toml; the main binary still resolves config.toml against its process CWD (scripts/e2e_shutdown.py:775-783; src/main.rs:14-33).
  • Reference appliance adds writable ephemeral /tmp despite wording that it has no writable volumes; no production proxy /tmp write consumer was found (docs/deployment.md:103-120; docs/alumina-proxy.md:163).
  • The test-temp finding requires a shared writable temporary directory and host rules permitting symlink following; no actual test-host policy or runner privilege was supplied (src/log/tests.rs:21-35).
  • Document/config discrepancy: docs/deployment.md:116-120 says the host-network appliance binds 0.0.0.0:5353, but its Dockerfile copies an unspecified operator config and the supplied example binds 127.0.0.1:5353. Code binds the parsed value exactly (docs/deployment.md:60-66; docs/qa-package/config.example.toml:1-4; src/config/mod.rs:1184-1202; src/runtime/storage.rs:1658-1663).
  • Example resolver pins are explicitly placeholders; if copied unchanged, pinned DoT should fail identity checks. Actual pins are absent (docs/qa-package/config.example.toml:15-30; src/dns/transport.rs:810-823).
  • Documented systemd/image workflow is illustrative with placeholder registry and digest. Actual signing, account, image, firewall effect and config artifact are unverified (docs/deployment.md:45-114).
  • No operator config.toml, installed appliance, firewall, actual resolver, image, or stdout collector is supplied. The VPC pattern is conditional (README.md:92-105; docs/deployment.md:45-114).
  • Local example binds 127.0.0.1:5353; dedicated appliance describes 0.0.0.0:5353; binary binds configured value (docs/qa-package/config.example.toml:1-4; docs/deployment.md:116-120; src/runtime/storage.rs:1658-1663).
  • Example calls unpinned IP#fqdn CA-chain validating, but empty-root implementation fails closed; README and governing spec state this (docs/qa-package/config.example.toml:8-13; src/dns/transport.rs:784-832; README.md:51-55; docs/alumina-proxy.md:113).
  • Root-validating/no-stale policy is an operator declaration; proxy cannot establish resolver trust anchors, clock, or no-stale behavior (src/config/mod.rs:631-643,678-690; README.md:64-73).
  • Pinned DoT certificate validity-window mismatch warns while matching pin is accepted, expressly documented (src/dns/transport.rs:801-823; docs/alumina-proxy.md:1198-1202,1538-1542).
  • Config loader reads <cwd>/config.toml (src/main.rs:19-31; src/config/mod.rs:537-558); documented scratch container reads /config.toml via WORKDIR / and COPY (docs/deployment.md:45-73,96-103).
  • Bare-IP DNS uses <configured IP>:53 over plain TCP; unpinned FQDN uses <configured IP>:853 with empty roots; strict-pinned FQDN uses <configured IP>:853 with name and pin checks (src/dns/resolver.rs:184-230; src/dns/transport.rs:801-832,1674-1691,3199-3214).
  • Telemetry uses inherited stdout fd 1 and bounded nonblocking queue; actual sink/collector is deployment-owned. Appliance example uses Docker gcplogs (src/log/mod.rs:633-648; src/log/sink.rs:9-26; docs/deployment.md:96-104; docs/monitoring.md:3-9).
  • Documented privileged image workflow uses /var/lib/docker/.docker registry credentials and digest-pinned pull; installed unit and grants absent (docs/deployment.md:75-114).
  • Boot fixture clobber requires a shared writable test temp directory, predictable placement of the PID/counter directory and config.toml symlink, relevant native tests, and a runner-writable target; no test-host policy was supplied (tests/support/temp_dir.rs:8-24).
  • Host benchmark temp-path clobber requires execution in a shared writable host /tmp with a runner-writable target; containerized self-test or private temp directories remove that cross-user path.
  • Shutdown E2E log clobber requires a shared writable /tmp namespace, a planted fixed-name path, a runner-writable target, and permitted symlink following.
  • The documented appliance is x86_64; no supported 32-bit deployment or 2^21-reuse reproduction was shown (docs/deployment.md:58; src/runtime/reactor.rs:3399-3406).

[1] JA4 block leaves the triggering tunnel able to send data

Field Value
Severity medium
Confidence high
Confidence rationale The source shows the ordering and all block-scope branches directly. Runtime reproduction was not run, and actual deployment configuration is unknown.
Category Security control bypass
CWE CWE-693
Affected lines src/runtime/reactor.rs:2847-2854, src/runtime/reactor.rs:2935-2943, src/runtime/reactor.rs:2885-2898, src/runtime/reactor.rs:2415-2428, src/runtime/reactor.rs:2371-2379, src/enforcement/state.rs:351-369

Summary

After the 16-entry JA4 baseline for an allowlisted destination is full, a client can send a new accepted ClientHello and continue sending through the triggering tunnel despite a configured ja4 block with connection or fqdn scope. hello_complete() flushes buffered bytes before evaluating the JA4 change, and the block handler does not close that slot for either scope.

Root Cause

hello_complete() validates the ClientHello and flushes the buffered tunnel to the upstream socket before calling maybe_record_ja4_baseline(). When a full JA4 set yields Ja4Change, project_tripwire() only handles All and Domain; Connection has no current-slot close, while stop_domain_block() explicitly excludes the current slot. Thus a configured block does not stop the offending tunnel, and its bytes can already be sent.

fn record(&mut self, ordinal: DomainOrdinal, ja4: [u8; 36]) -> BaselineOutcome {
    let row = &mut self.entries[ordinal.get()];
    for entry in row.iter() {
        if entry.ja4 == ja4 {
            return BaselineOutcome::Unchanged;
        }

    for entry in row.iter_mut() {
        if entry.ja4 == [0; 36] {
            *entry = Ja4BaselineEntry { ja4 };
            return BaselineOutcome::FirstSeen;
        }
    }
    BaselineOutcome::Overflow
}

Specified block semantics — docs/alumina-proxy.md:309-311

The governing specification requires connection block to terminate the offender and domain block to affect current matching flows.

- **Block Connection:** terminates the offender connection only; no scope history.
- **Block Domain:** a fixed ordinal table (at most 32 entries) marks the configured domain blocked; it affects current and future flows matching that ordinal until restart.
- **Block All:** synchronously prevents all subsequent application I/O, including pending writes and new admission, before any further I/O, then performs bounded physical closure of at most 512 slots.

Validation

The inspected call sequence confirms accepted client bytes reach the socket before the JA4 decision, and Connection/Domain block branches cannot close the triggering slot. The spec explicitly says both scopes must affect it.

Specified block semantics — docs/alumina-proxy.md:309-311

The governing specification requires connection block to terminate the offender and domain block to affect current matching flows.

- **Block Connection:** terminates the offender connection only; no scope history.
- **Block Domain:** a fixed ordinal table (at most 32 entries) marks the configured domain blocked; it affects current and future flows matching that ordinal until restart.
- **Block All:** synchronously prevents all subsequent application I/O, including pending writes and new admission, before any further I/O, then performs bounded physical closure of at most 512 slots.

Assertions:

  • The JA4 change path is reachable only after the per-ordinal set fills with 16 distinct accepted values.
  • connection scope falls through the block handler without closing the slot.
  • fqdn scope latches future denial and closes other same-ordinal slots, but excludes the offender.
  • all scope closes the offender after the prior flush.
  • An independent baseline reviewer separately traced the same ordering and current-slot omission.

Counterevidence and remaining uncertainty:

  • The attack remains limited to an allowlisted destination and currently admissible DNS address.
  • The default JA4 change requires 16 existing distinct baseline values; ordinary first-seen values do not trigger a block.
  • An all scope block does close the triggering slot after the flush.

Limitations:

  • No runtime reproduction or actual deployed configuration was available.

Dataflow

ClientHello bytes -> inspector -> hello_complete() -> upstream socket write -> JA4 overflow decision -> incomplete block handling -> live tunnel

  • Source: Client-controlled initial TLS ClientHello and following tunnel bytes

  • Sink: Upstream TCP socket and persistent relay slot

  • Outcome: Configured JA4 block does not stop the triggering tunnel

Reachability

A listener-reachable client can trigger the path when the chosen allowlist entry has ja4 = { action = "block", scope = "connection" | "fqdn" } and its JA4 set has been filled with 16 distinct accepted fingerprints. No config-edit authority is required of the client; reaching the listener depends on deployment networking.

  • Attacker: Compromised application or other listener-reachable client

  • Entry point: HTTP CONNECT followed by an accepted initial TLS ClientHello

  • Outcome: Offender can continue sending to an admitted endpoint despite the block decision

Preconditions:

  • Configured JA4 block with connection or fqdn scope
  • 16 distinct JA4 baseline values already stored for the same allowlist ordinal
  • An admissible DNS binding and reachable upstream endpoint

Limitations:

  • The proxy still restricts the destination to an allowlisted hostname:port and eligible DNS address.

Severity

Medium — A compromised proxy client can bypass an operator-selected JA4 block and keep an admitted egress tunnel, potentially using an allowed endpoint for further exfiltration. It requires a full 16-value JA4 set and a block action with connection or fqdn scope; destinations remain constrained by the allowlist and DNS checks.

Severity would rise if this configuration protects a high-value reachable endpoint and clients can readily fill the JA4 set; it would fall if only notify or all-scope actions are deployed.

Impact assessment:

  • Level: high
  • Why: An operator-selected block can fail to stop an egress tunnel, allowing continued traffic to an admitted endpoint.

Likelihood assessment:

  • Level: medium
  • Why: The client must first fill the JA4 set and the operator must configure the affected block scope.

Remediation

Evaluate and enforce JA4 change before the first upstream flush. For every Effect::Block, close the triggering slot; for domain and all scopes, additionally preserve the current latches and close the other affected slots before any further I/O.

Tests:

  • Fill the JA4 baseline with 16 accepted variants, trigger a 17th under connection block, and assert the offender socket closes before any ClientHello or trailing payload reaches upstream.
  • Repeat with fqdn and all scopes, asserting the triggering slot and all required sibling slots close and no post-decision bytes are written.

Preventive controls:

  • Centralize block-scope handling so every block effect closes the triggering slot before applying wider scope state.

Summary

After 16 distinct JA4 fingerprints fill an allowed domain’s baseline, a client can send a 17th valid fingerprint on an allowlisted CONNECT. The reactor forwards the validated ClientHello and potentially buffered trailing bytes before evaluating the configured JA4 block. Block Connection records an effect but never closes the triggering slot; Block Domain latches the domain and closes other matching slots while exempting the offender. The triggering slot can advance to Relay and continue upstream exchange. Block All closes slots after the decision, so bytes forwarded before that decision remain a timing consequence of the same order.

Root Cause

The JA4 block decision follows the first upstream flush of the validated ClientHello and potentially buffered trailing bytes. If that write closes the slot, inspector reset can suppress recording the change. Once overflow is projected, Connection scope has no offender-close branch and Domain scope closes matching siblings while exempting the triggering slot; the active slot can enter Relay. Block All closes slots after its decision but cannot retract bytes already sent.

    match effect {
        Effect::Notify { .. } => {
            self.monitor.note_action_notify(ordinal);
        }
        Effect::Block { scope } => {
            self.monitor.note_action_domain_block(ordinal);

Assertions:

  • JA4 overflow is reachable after 16 distinct fingerprints for one approved ordinal.
  • Connection and Domain block effects leave the triggering slot open.
  • All scope closes the triggering slot and is not affected.
  • The 16-entry baseline returns Overflow for the next distinct fingerprint.
  • The configured ja4 action can be block with connection or fqdn scope.
  • The triggering slot is omitted from both closure branches and can remain in relay.
  • A failed first upstream write can reset the inspector before the later JA4 lookup records the change.
  • The JA4 baseline returns Overflow after 16 distinct values for a domain (src/runtime/reactor.rs:600-619).
  • The JA4 control can be Block with Connection, Domain, or All scope (src/config/mod.rs:985-1015).
  • hello_complete flushes before JA4 evaluation (src/runtime/reactor.rs:2853-2854).
  • project_tripwire omits Connection closure and excludes the triggering slot from Domain closure (src/runtime/reactor.rs:2415-2427,2371-2379).
  • Config accepts JA4 Block Connection/Domain/All at src/config/mod.rs:985-1015.
  • The baseline stores 16 entries per ordinal at src/runtime/reactor.rs:578-615.
  • The domain latch is set at src/enforcement/state.rs:356-367; future CONNECTs are rejected at src/runtime/reactor.rs:2476-2481.

Counterevidence and remaining uncertainty:

  • The CONNECT host and TLS SNI still must match the allowlist; the flaw affects a configured JA4 block, not general destination authorization.
  • Block All closes all slots after its threshold, but the first upstream write may already have occurred.
  • Exact CONNECT hostname and port authorization still applies; the bypass does not grant arbitrary egress.
  • Block(All) closes slots after the JA4 decision, limiting that scope to bytes forwarded before the decision.
  • Only an exact allowlisted pair and successfully validated ClientHello reaches this path (src/runtime/reactor.rs:2450-2522,2825-2850).
  • The first 16 distinct JA4 values seed the baseline (src/runtime/reactor.rs:600-619).
  • The proxy relays to an approved endpoint and does not decrypt later payloads (README.md:22-25,48-50).
  • Block All closes live slots through src/runtime/reactor.rs:2355-2365.
  • Domain latch blocks later matching CONNECT at src/runtime/reactor.rs:2473-2481.
  • Change signal requires a full 16-entry baseline and is suppressed by Ignore (src/runtime/reactor.rs:600-619,2891-2901).
  • The ClientHello must first pass profile, SNI, and exact allowlist checks (src/inspection/client_hello.rs:874-886; src/runtime/reactor.rs:2450-2522).
  • All-scope block closes slots after the decision; domain latch rejects future matching connections (src/runtime/reactor.rs:2355-2365,2472-2480).
  • Malformed CONNECT or ClientHello is rejected before forwarding.
  • Block All closes all active slots after its effect; the pre-decision flush remains.
  • Future CONNECT attempts for a blocked domain are refused; the already active triggering slot is not rechecked.

  • Real-world impact depends on an actual listener, configured JA4 Block action, and capabilities of an approved endpoint.

            self.monitor.note_action_domain_block(ordinal);

Reachability

Requires listener access, an approved CONNECT hostname and port with a current eligible DNS binding and matching valid SNI, a configured JA4 Block Connection or Domain policy, and 16 distinct accepted fingerprints for the same domain ordinal. The 17th distinct fingerprint triggers the block while the initiating tunnel can continue relaying.

  • Attacker: compromised application client with listener access

  • Entry point: CONNECT and initial TLS ClientHello

  • Outcome: continued traffic on the triggering tunnel after the block

Preconditions:

  • Proxy is deployed and reachable by the adversarial workload.
  • An allowlisted domain has JA4 configured to block at connection or domain scope.
  • The per-ordinal baseline contains 16 distinct fingerprints; the next is new.
  • An allowed hostname and current eligible DNS binding exist.
  • The operator configured ja4 block with connection or domain scope.
  • The attacker can send enough distinct valid ClientHello variants to fill the 16-value baseline.
  • Allowlisted FQDN:port and eligible DNS binding
  • JA4 block configured for the allowlist entry
  • 16 distinct accepted JA4 fingerprints previously seeded for that ordinal

Existing controls:

  • Exact CONNECT allowlist and matching SNI still apply.
  • All-scope block closes all slots.
  • Domain scope blocks future and other current flows.
  • The CONNECT host and TLS SNI still must match the allowlist; this is a JA4 policy bypass rather than general destination authorization.
  • Exact allowlist pair and SNI/TLS profile check still hold.
  • Block All works; Domain latch blocks future connections.

Severity

Medium — Configured JA4 Block Connection or Domain can leave the triggering approved-destination tunnel active, and all block scopes can forward buffered bytes before the decision. Exploitation needs listener access, an allowlisted hostname with usable binding, 16 seeded distinct fingerprints for that ordinal, and a 17th valid SNI-matching ClientHello. The approved destination restriction remains, and deployment impact is unknown.

Severity rises if the approved endpoint exposes high-value capabilities and JA4 block is relied on for containment; it falls if only Notify or Ignore is configured or the listener is unreachable.

Impact assessment:

  • Level: medium
  • Why: The security tripwire fails to terminate the anomalous flow, but the destination remains restricted to the approved endpoint.

Likelihood assessment:

  • Level: medium
  • Why: After baseline saturation, the control-flow bypass is deterministic; setup and configuration prerequisites narrow exposure.

Remediation

Evaluate and record JA4 overflow immediately after ClientHello validation, before flushing the Hello or any buffered trailing bytes. Apply the configured action before upstream I/O and retain the change signal if a subsequent write fails. Close the triggering slot for Block Connection and Block Domain; for Domain also close siblings and latch future matching flows, and for All close all slots. Make the caller stop processing a closed slot.

Tests:

  • Configure JA4 Block Connection; saturate one ordinal's baseline and verify the triggering slot closes before any upstream write.
  • Repeat with JA4 Block Domain and verify the triggering slot, sibling flows, and future flows are blocked.
  • Confirm Notify and All actions retain their intended behavior.
  • With ja4 = { action = "block", scope = "connection" }, fill the baseline and verify the 17th distinct ClientHello closes its own tunnel before bytes reach upstream.
  • With scope = "fqdn", verify the triggering and sibling tunnels close and later CONNECT requests for that ordinal are refused.
  • With scope = "all", verify no pending client bytes are sent after the block decision.
  • Seed 16 distinct accepted JA4s, configure Block All, send a 17th fingerprint with pipelined application bytes, and assert no bytes reach upstream before the block.
  • Force an upstream write failure and assert the JA4 change signal is still retained.
  • Seed 16 distinct JA4 fingerprints, trigger a 17th under Block Connection, and assert the current tunnel closes before relay.
  • Repeat under Block Domain and assert both the triggering and other current matching tunnels close, while future matching CONNECT requests are refused.
  • Verify Block All and notify/ignore behavior remain correct.
  • After seeding 16 distinct JA4s, assert a 17th with Block Connection sends no tunnel bytes and closes its slot.
  • Repeat for Block Domain, asserting the offender and all existing same-domain slots close, while unrelated domains remain active.
  • Assert Block All still closes all slots and Notify still permits relay.
  • Fill the JA4 baseline and trigger Block Connection and Block Domain with a 17th distinct accepted ClientHello; assert the offender closes and cannot relay more bytes.
  • Assert Block Domain also closes current sibling tunnels and refuses subsequent CONNECT attempts.
  • Seed 16 JA4 fingerprints, send a 17th accepted Hello plus buffered following bytes to a writable loopback upstream, and assert no bytes arrive when any JA4 Block scope is configured.
  • With a full JA4 baseline, exercise a valid distinct ClientHello against a connected upstream for each Block scope and assert the offending socket closes and sends no tunnel bytes.
  • Verify notify and ignore keep their documented behavior and existing allowlist/SNI checks still apply.
  • With 16 distinct baseline fingerprints, send a 17th valid ClientHello and assert Block Connection closes that socket before the upstream receives bytes.
  • Repeat for Block Domain, asserting the triggering and other matching tunnels close while future CONNECTs are rejected.
  • Repeat for Block All and assert no buffered post-hello payload is sent before the global latch.

Preventive controls:

  • Centralize effect application so every Block scope has an explicit current-slot outcome.
  • Make action projection return a typed continue-or-close decision that every event-loop caller must handle before forwarding.
  • Centralize physical closure for every Block effect and make the triggering slot an explicit operand of scoped enforcement.
  • Test JA4 actions through the real serving path, including the triggering slot and upstream byte count.

[3] JA4 block lets buffered client bytes reach the upstream first

Field Value
Severity medium
Confidence high
Confidence rationale Static source order shows flush_client_upstream and its socket write precede maybe_record_ja4_baseline; the 17th distinct JA4 selects the configured effect. No runtime execution was performed.
Category JA4 block enforced after upstream forwarding
CWE CWE-863
Affected lines src/runtime/reactor.rs:2853, src/runtime/reactor.rs:2937, src/runtime/reactor.rs:2897, src/runtime/reactor.rs:605, src/config/mod.rs:1006, docs/alumina-proxy.md:309

Summary

After 16 distinct JA4 values have filled an allowlisted domain’s baseline, a client can send a 17th valid ClientHello and buffered follow-on bytes. hello_complete() writes those bytes upstream before it evaluates the configured JA4 Block, so even an eventual All-scope closure occurs after the write.

Root Cause

The JA4 action is evaluated after the first upstream drain. hello_complete validates SNI and calls flush_client_upstream before recording the JA4; the drain writes the retained buffer to the upstream socket. Only then can an overflowing baseline invoke project_tripwire, so a configured Block cannot prevent that write.

Documented block semantics — docs/alumina-proxy.md:307-312

The documented policy promises that applied blocks terminate matching current traffic.

### Block and Notify semantics

- **Block Connection:** terminates the offender connection only; no scope history.
- **Block Domain:** a fixed ordinal table (at most 32 entries) marks the configured domain blocked; it affects current and future flows matching that ordinal until restart.
- **Block All:** synchronously prevents all subsequent application I/O, including pending writes and new admission, before any further I/O, then performs bounded physical closure of at most 512 slots. It persists until restart; there is no runtime unblock interface.
- **Notify** (renamed from `flare_only`): a notification and aggregation context only. It never authorizes forwarding, never delays baseline denial, and never widens scope. Implicit Notify for an applied Block inherits that Block's scope (reporting scope equals enforcement scope).

Validation

A full JA4 baseline produces Overflow; the validated hello path sends buffered client bytes through up.write before maybe_record_ja4_baseline selects a configured Block. SNI/profile validation precedes this write, and the first 16 values intentionally seed the table.

Reachability

Requires access to the proxy listener, an allowlisted hostname with a current DNS binding, and a configured JA4 Block for that domain. The client can vary valid ClientHello metadata; the 17th distinct fingerprint triggers overflow. All-scope effect additionally requires its gate threshold.

  • Attacker: Compromised or malicious proxy client

  • Entry point: Plain HTTP CONNECT followed by TLS ClientHello

  • Outcome: First buffered bytes reach the approved upstream before a configured block can stop them

Preconditions:

  • Allowed destination and live binding
  • Configured JA4 Block
  • Sixteen prior distinct JA4 baselines for the same ordinal

Severity

Medium — A compromised workload that can reach an allowed destination can deliberately vary valid ClientHello fields and trigger a configured JA4 Block. The premature write defeats the intended block for bytes already sent, but the destination remains allowlisted and the consequence is bounded to data sent before the effect applies.

Raise severity if a demonstrated deployed configuration uses Block All to protect sensitive upstream commands or data that fit in the first buffered write; lower it if JA4 blocking is not configured or no upstream write can occur before the effect.

Impact assessment:

  • Level: medium
  • Why: Configured block is bypassed for the first buffered write to an approved destination.

Likelihood assessment:

  • Level: medium
  • Why: Attacker needs control of valid ClientHello variants and 17 connection attempts to one configured domain.

Remediation

Evaluate and apply JA4 Block immediately after successful ClientHello validation and before any buffered client bytes are written upstream; cover both pipelined and deferred dial paths.

Tests:

  • Seed 16 distinct valid JA4 fingerprints, then assert that the 17th with Block Connection sends zero tunnel bytes upstream.
  • Repeat with Block Domain and an All-scope threshold crossing, including ClientHello plus coalesced bytes and a WouldBlock write path.

Preventive controls:

  • Keep tripwire evaluation before the first I/O it is intended to stop, with assertions at the reactor transition.

Summary

After 16 distinct JA4 fingerprints fill an allowed domain’s baseline, a client can send a 17th valid fingerprint on an allowlisted CONNECT. If the upstream is already connected when the ClientHello completes, the reactor can forward the validated Hello and buffered trailing bytes before evaluating the configured JA4 block. If the Hello completes before dial, JA4 projection occurs on successful dial before that first forwarding. In either order, Block Connection records an effect but never closes the triggering slot; Block Domain latches the domain and closes other matching slots while exempting the offender. The triggering slot can advance to Relay and continue upstream exchange. Block All closes slots after the decision, so its pre-decision byte leak requires the upstream-connected ordering. The latest source trace confirms that the first flush can write through the full buffered segment, including bytes after the validated Hello; a Block All verdict cannot retract those bytes. A particular write may be partial or WouldBlock, and TLS 1.3 early-data acceptance is upstream dependent. An all-scope block requires the configured JA4 gate threshold to be crossed; earlier overflows can be baseline-only. The pre-decision write is bounded by the 64 KiB live-visit I/O limit and depends on buffer occupancy and socket writability.

Root Cause

JA4 classification is invoked after the first attempted upstream flush. When the upstream is already connected, that flush can send the validated ClientHello and buffered trailing bytes before the decision; if it fails and closes the slot, inspector reset can suppress recording the change. Once overflow is projected, Connection scope has no offender-close branch and Domain scope closes matching siblings while exempting the triggering slot; the active slot can enter Relay. Block All closes slots after its decision but cannot retract bytes already sent. The all-scope gate can turn an overflow into BaselineOnly until its threshold is crossed; when crossed, the preceding drain may write through buf_len, beyond the validated Hello end, subject to the live-visit I/O cap.

fn stop_domain_block(&mut self, ordinal: DomainOrdinal, except: usize) {
    for index in 0..self.slots.len() {
        if index != except
            && self.slots[index].stage != Stage::Idle
            && self.slots[index].stage != Stage::Closing
            && self.slot_ordinal(index) == Some(ordinal)
        {
            self.close_slot(index);
        }
    }
}

Enforcement state only latches broader scopes — src/enforcement/state.rs:351-368

The action state records the block but has no per-connection termination; that must occur in the reactor, which currently omits it.

const fn apply_per_fqdn_action(&mut self, effect: Effect, ordinal: DomainOrdinal) {
    match effect {
        Effect::Notify { .. } => {
            self.monitor.note_action_notify(ordinal);
        }
        Effect::Block { scope } => {
            self.monitor.note_action_domain_block(ordinal);
            match scope {
                Scope::Domain => self.blocked |= 1 << ordinal.get(),
                Scope::All => {
                    let was_latched = self.block_all;
                    self.block_all = true;
                    if !was_latched {
                        self.monitor.note_block_all();
                    }
                }
                Scope::Connection => {}
            }
        }

The pre-action flush can move the slot to Relay and send further buffered bytes; later relay handlers check only the all-scope latch.

    fn flush_client_upstream(&mut self, index: usize) {
        let (written, failed) = self.drain_to_upstream(index);
        if failed {
            self.close_slot(index);
            return;
        }
        let was_open = self.slots[index].gate.is_open();
        if written == 0 || was_open {
            self.slots[index].relay_cursor_reset();
            if self.visit_exhausted(index) {
                self.reschedule(index, RescheduleArm::Upstream);
            }
            return;
        }
        let outcome = self.slots[index].gate.upstream_write(written);
        if matches!(
            outcome,
            UpstreamWrite::GateOpened { .. } | UpstreamWrite::Open
        ) {
            if self.slots[index].tunnel.is_none() {
                let slot = self.slots[index].handle.take();
                if let Some(slot) = slot {
                    let tunnel = self.storage.finish_setup(slot);
                    self.slots[index].tunnel = Some(tunnel);
                    self.note_occupancy(Instant::now());
                }
            }
            self.apply_slot_deadline(index, |ws| {
                ws.setup_deadline = None;
                ws.idle_deadline = Some(Instant::now() + IDLE_SECS);
                ws.stage = Stage::Relay;
            });
            let (written2, failed2) = self.drain_to_upstream(index);
            if failed2 {
                self.close_slot(index);
                return;
            }
            if written2 > 0 {
                self.slots[index].gate.upstream_write(written2);
            }
        }

JA4 block scopes are configurable — src/config/mod.rs:983-1015

The operator can configure JA4 Block with connection, domain, or all scope; the flaw affects the two narrower block choices.

/// Parses one per-FQDN control value (`early_data` or `ja4`): either the bare
/// `"ignore"` opt-out shorthand or a `{ action, scope }` table with `action`
/// in `notify|block` (tarpit reserved) and `scope` in `connection|fqdn|all`.
/// For `early_data` the only legal `block` scope is `connection`; `fqdn` and
/// `all` block scopes are invalid configuration (docs F-02 close), so an
/// upstream-sourced early-data signal cannot select a per-domain or
/// process-wide latch. `ja4` keeps the full scope grammar unchanged.
fn parse_per_fqdn_control(
    value: &toml::Value,
    fqdn_key: &str,
    control_key: &str,
) -> Result<PerFqdnControl, ConfigError> {
    let prefix = format!("allowed_fqdn.{fqdn_key}.{control_key}");
    match value {
        toml::Value::String(action) => match action.as_str() {
            "ignore" => Ok(PerFqdnControl::ignore()),
            "tarpit" => Err(ConfigError::ActionTarpitDeferred { key: prefix }),
            other => Err(ConfigError::UnknownAction {
                key: prefix,
                value: other.to_owned(),
            }),
        },
        toml::Value::Table(table) => {
            let (kind, scope_text) = read_action_scope_table(table, &prefix)?;
            let scope = parse_per_fqdn_scope(&scope_text, &format!("{prefix}.scope"))?;
            if control_key == "early_data"
                && kind == ActionKind::Block
                && scope != Scope::Connection
            {
                return Err(ConfigError::EarlyDataBlockScopeInvalid { scope: scope_text });
            }
            Ok(PerFqdnControl::control(kind, scope))
        }

Documented block behavior — docs/alumina-proxy.md:309-311

The governing specification requires connection block to terminate the offender and domain block to affect current and future flows.

- **Block Connection:** terminates the offender connection only; no scope history.
- **Block Domain:** a fixed ordinal table (at most 32 entries) marks the configured domain blocked; it affects current and future flows matching that ordinal until restart.
- **Block All:** synchronously prevents all subsequent application I/O, including pending writes and new admission, before any further I/O, then performs bounded physical closure of at most 512 slots. It persists until restart; there is no runtime unblock interface.

    fn drain_to_upstream(&mut self, index: usize) -> (usize, bool) {
        let secs = self.storage.cache_secs(Instant::now());
        let mut written = 0;

Per-visit I/O is bounded — src/runtime/reactor.rs:2046-2058

A live visit caps byte work at 64 KiB, narrowing the pre-decision send.

    /// The byte room left in `index`'s live visit; `default` when the visit is
    /// not live, so a single read/write slice can never push a live visit past
    /// the canonical 64 KiB bound.
    fn io_room(&self, index: usize, default: usize) -> usize {
        if let VisitState::Live { slot, bytes, .. } = self.visit
            && slot == index
        {
            (VISIT_BYTES as usize)
                .saturating_sub(bytes as usize)
                .min(default)
        } else {
            default
        }

Validation

Static source traces establish a reachable 17th distinct valid JA4 overflow, first upstream forwarding before the action, and no triggering-slot closure for Connection or Domain scope. Domain latches and closes siblings; All closes slots only after the decision. No runtime reproduction or deployed JA4 configuration was available. The newest source trace also establishes that a write failure can reset the inspector before the JA4 signal is recorded. The assigned source finding independently confirms that operator configuration accepts connection and fqdn scopes and that the future-CONNECT domain precheck cannot close the triggering tunnel. The assigned worker independently confirmed the accepted configuration scopes, overflow threshold, forwarding order, offender-excluding domain sweep, and continued relay. This worker clarified that the pre-decision byte leak requires an upstream connection before Hello completion; the offender-closure gap remains under either ordering. A separate trace confirms the first flush may include the full buffered segment and that actual bytes written depend on socket readiness. This worker corroborated the triggering-slot bypass and showed that all-scope JA4 blocks require a gate-threshold crossing; a pre-decision drain uses buf_len and is capped per live visit.

Flush can establish a relay — src/runtime/reactor.rs:2975-3015

The pre-action flush can move the slot to Relay and send further buffered bytes; later relay handlers check only the all-scope latch.

    fn flush_client_upstream(&mut self, index: usize) {
        let (written, failed) = self.drain_to_upstream(index);
        if failed {
            self.close_slot(index);
            return;
        }
        let was_open = self.slots[index].gate.is_open();
        if written == 0 || was_open {
            self.slots[index].relay_cursor_reset();
            if self.visit_exhausted(index) {
                self.reschedule(index, RescheduleArm::Upstream);
            }
            return;
        }
        let outcome = self.slots[index].gate.upstream_write(written);
        if matches!(
            outcome,
            UpstreamWrite::GateOpened { .. } | UpstreamWrite::Open
        ) {
            if self.slots[index].tunnel.is_none() {
                let slot = self.slots[index].handle.take();
                if let Some(slot) = slot {
                    let tunnel = self.storage.finish_setup(slot);
                    self.slots[index].tunnel = Some(tunnel);
                    self.note_occupancy(Instant::now());
                }
            }
            self.apply_slot_deadline(index, |ws| {
                ws.setup_deadline = None;
                ws.idle_deadline = Some(Instant::now() + IDLE_SECS);
                ws.stage = Stage::Relay;
            });
            let (written2, failed2) = self.drain_to_upstream(index);
            if failed2 {
                self.close_slot(index);
                return;
            }
            if written2 > 0 {
                self.slots[index].gate.upstream_write(written2);
            }
        }

        for entry in row.iter() {
            if entry.ja4 == ja4 {
                return BaselineOutcome::Unchanged;
            }
        }
        for entry in row.iter_mut() {
            if entry.ja4 == [0; 36] {
                *entry = Ja4BaselineEntry { ja4 };
                return BaselineOutcome::FirstSeen;
            }
        }
        BaselineOutcome::Overflow
    }

JA4 block scopes are configurable — src/config/mod.rs:983-1015

The operator can configure JA4 Block with connection, domain, or all scope; the flaw affects the two narrower block choices.

/// Parses one per-FQDN control value (`early_data` or `ja4`): either the bare
/// `"ignore"` opt-out shorthand or a `{ action, scope }` table with `action`
/// in `notify|block` (tarpit reserved) and `scope` in `connection|fqdn|all`.
/// For `early_data` the only legal `block` scope is `connection`; `fqdn` and
/// `all` block scopes are invalid configuration (docs F-02 close), so an
/// upstream-sourced early-data signal cannot select a per-domain or
/// process-wide latch. `ja4` keeps the full scope grammar unchanged.
fn parse_per_fqdn_control(
    value: &toml::Value,
    fqdn_key: &str,
    control_key: &str,
) -> Result<PerFqdnControl, ConfigError> {
    let prefix = format!("allowed_fqdn.{fqdn_key}.{control_key}");
    match value {
        toml::Value::String(action) => match action.as_str() {
            "ignore" => Ok(PerFqdnControl::ignore()),
            "tarpit" => Err(ConfigError::ActionTarpitDeferred { key: prefix }),
            other => Err(ConfigError::UnknownAction {
                key: prefix,
                value: other.to_owned(),
            }),
        },
        toml::Value::Table(table) => {
            let (kind, scope_text) = read_action_scope_table(table, &prefix)?;
            let scope = parse_per_fqdn_scope(&scope_text, &format!("{prefix}.scope"))?;
            if control_key == "early_data"
                && kind == ActionKind::Block
                && scope != Scope::Connection
            {
                return Err(ConfigError::EarlyDataBlockScopeInvalid { scope: scope_text });
            }
            Ok(PerFqdnControl::control(kind, scope))
        }

Documented block semantics — docs/alumina-proxy.md:309-310

The configured block semantics require termination of the offender and, for domain scope, current matching flows.

- **Block Connection:** terminates the offender connection only; no scope history.
- **Block Domain:** a fixed ordinal table (at most 32 entries) marks the configured domain blocked; it affects current and future flows matching that ordinal until restart.

    fn hello_complete(&mut self, index: usize) {
        let Some(approved) = self.slots[index].approved else {
            self.project_tripwire(index, Violation::MissingParseResult);
            self.close_slot(index);
            return;
        };
        let verdict = self.slots[index]
            .inspector
            .hello()

            Some(Ok(accepted)) => accepted,

                self.close_slot(index);
                return;
            }

        let end = ws.head_len + ws.hello_consumed;
        ws.gate
            .on_hello_validated(ValidatedHello::new(accepted, end));
        ws.stage = Stage::WritingHello;
        ws.fwd = ws.head_len - ws.buf_base;

Per-visit I/O is bounded — src/runtime/reactor.rs:2046-2058

A live visit caps byte work at 64 KiB, narrowing the pre-decision send.

    /// The byte room left in `index`'s live visit; `default` when the visit is
    /// not live, so a single read/write slice can never push a live visit past
    /// the canonical 64 KiB bound.
    fn io_room(&self, index: usize, default: usize) -> usize {
        if let VisitState::Live { slot, bytes, .. } = self.visit
            && slot == index
        {
            (VISIT_BYTES as usize)
                .saturating_sub(bytes as usize)
                .min(default)
        } else {
            default
        }

Assertions:

  • JA4 overflow is reachable after 16 distinct fingerprints for one approved ordinal.
  • Connection and Domain block effects leave the triggering slot open.
  • All scope closes the triggering slot and is not affected.
  • The 16-entry baseline returns Overflow for the next distinct fingerprint.
  • The configured ja4 action can be block with connection or fqdn scope.
  • The triggering slot is omitted from both closure branches and can remain in relay.
  • A failed first upstream write can reset the inspector before the later JA4 lookup records the change.
  • The JA4 baseline returns Overflow after 16 distinct values for a domain (src/runtime/reactor.rs:600-619).
  • The JA4 control can be Block with Connection, Domain, or All scope (src/config/mod.rs:985-1015).
  • hello_complete flushes before JA4 evaluation (src/runtime/reactor.rs:2853-2854).
  • project_tripwire omits Connection closure and excludes the triggering slot from Domain closure (src/runtime/reactor.rs:2415-2427,2371-2379).
  • Config accepts JA4 Block Connection/Domain/All at src/config/mod.rs:985-1015.
  • The baseline stores 16 entries per ordinal at src/runtime/reactor.rs:578-615.
  • The domain latch is set at src/enforcement/state.rs:356-367; future CONNECTs are rejected at src/runtime/reactor.rs:2476-2481.
  • The configured JA4 block scope can be Connection or Domain.
  • A new JA4 after sixteen distinct values triggers Overflow.
  • No connection-scope branch closes the offender; domain closure explicitly skips it.
  • Connection and fqdn/domain block scopes are accepted for JA4.
  • Overflow follows 16 distinct baseline JA4 values.
  • The accepted hello is flushed before JA4 policy evaluation.
  • The only latch check for a blocked domain occurs on a new CONNECT decision.
  • Client input is buffered and a complete hello invokes hello_complete.
  • hello_complete calls flush_client_upstream before maybe_record_ja4_baseline.
  • drain_to_upstream writes through buf_len, including trailing bytes.
  • JA4 overflow applies the block after the write.
  • The first upstream flush writes through buf_len, not the validated ClientHello end, so coalesced trailing bytes can reach a writable upstream before the JA4 verdict.

Counterevidence and remaining uncertainty:

  • The CONNECT host and TLS SNI still must match the allowlist; the flaw affects a configured JA4 block, not general destination authorization.
  • Block All closes all slots after its threshold, but the first upstream write may already have occurred.
  • Exact CONNECT hostname and port authorization still applies; the bypass does not grant arbitrary egress.
  • Block(All) closes slots after the JA4 decision, limiting that scope to bytes forwarded before the decision.
  • Only an exact allowlisted pair and successfully validated ClientHello reaches this path (src/runtime/reactor.rs:2450-2522,2825-2850).
  • The first 16 distinct JA4 values seed the baseline (src/runtime/reactor.rs:600-619).
  • The proxy relays to an approved endpoint and does not decrypt later payloads (README.md:22-25,48-50).
  • Block All closes live slots through src/runtime/reactor.rs:2355-2365.
  • Domain latch blocks later matching CONNECT at src/runtime/reactor.rs:2473-2481.
  • Change signal requires a full 16-entry baseline and is suppressed by Ignore (src/runtime/reactor.rs:600-619,2891-2901).
  • The ClientHello must first pass profile, SNI, and exact allowlist checks (src/inspection/client_hello.rs:874-886; src/runtime/reactor.rs:2450-2522).
  • All-scope block closes slots after the decision; domain latch rejects future matching connections (src/runtime/reactor.rs:2355-2365,2472-2480).
  • Malformed CONNECT or ClientHello is rejected before forwarding.
  • Block All closes all active slots after its effect; the pre-decision flush remains.
  • Future CONNECT attempts for a blocked domain are refused; the already active triggering slot is not rechecked.
  • Existing domain-latch test src/runtime/reactor/tests.rs:6676-6765 checks a later CONNECT but does not assert closure of the JA4-triggering slot.
  • The client must already satisfy exact hostname:port and ClientHello SNI checks.
  • Scope::All invokes stop_block_all and closes active slots; this finding targets connection and fqdn scopes.
  • The blocked-domain precheck at src/runtime/reactor.rs:2476-2482 protects future CONNECT requests, not an established triggering slot.
  • When ClientHello validation finishes before the upstream dial, JA4 projection runs on successful dial before first forwarding; the pre-decision byte leak requires an already connected upstream, while the Connection and Domain offender-closure gap remains.
  • All-scope block invokes stop_block_all and closes the triggering slot.
  • Early upstream data is separately a mandatory denial and does not establish JA4 closure.
  • JA4 cannot trigger on the first 16 distinct fingerprints in a domain row.
  • The ClientHello must pass TLS/SNI/ECH validation.
  • The upstream destination remains an approved numeric peer.
  • Live visit I/O is bounded at 64 KiB, and Block All closes slots after projection.
  • When the Hello completes before the dial, the JA4 verdict precedes that first upstream forwarding; the premature write requires the upstream-connected ordering.

Limitations:

  • No runtime reproduction was run.
  • Real-world impact depends on an actual listener, configured JA4 Block action, and capabilities of an approved endpoint.
  • Block All closes the triggering slot, although its first ClientHello write may have preceded the verdict.
  • Validated by source review without executing the proxy; no deployment configuration was supplied.
  • No runtime reproduction or actual operator configuration was supplied.
  • No runtime reproduction or actual operator configuration supplied.
  • No runtime test was executed.
  • No application execution or live socket reproduction was performed; current source suffices to establish branch behavior.
  • No runtime reproduction was executed; actual operator JA4 configuration and listener reachability are not supplied.
  • A specific socket write may be partial or WouldBlock, so the amount sent depends on readiness and kernel behavior.
  • TLS 1.3 early-data acceptance depends on the approved upstream and client session state; the ordering flaw does not depend on early-data acceptance.
  • No live deployment or runtime reproduction was available.
  • The impact remains confined to an already allowlisted destination and port.
  • No runtime reproduction or deployed configuration was available.
  • Amount of pre-decision traffic depends on buffer occupancy and socket writability.
  • No live socket reproduction was run; actual pre-decision delivery depends on write readiness and the configured JA4 action.

Dataflow

Client-controlled ClientHello and buffered trailing bytes -> validated Hello and JA4 fingerprint -> full per-domain baseline -> configured Block effect -> reactor closure switch omits triggering-slot close for Connection and Domain -> active upstream write and Relay. When upstream is already connected before Hello completion, the first flush can send bytes before the decision; a write failure can reset the inspector before recording the change.

  • Source: ClientHello bytes on approved CONNECT

  • Sink: upstream socket write from active tunnel

  • Outcome: Traffic continues after JA4 block action

const fn apply_per_fqdn_action(&mut self, effect: Effect, ordinal: DomainOrdinal) {
    match effect {
        Effect::Notify { .. } => {
            self.monitor.note_action_notify(ordinal);
        }
        Effect::Block { scope } => {
            self.monitor.note_action_domain_block(ordinal);
            match scope {
                Scope::Domain => self.blocked |= 1 << ordinal.get(),
                Scope::All => {
                    let was_latched = self.block_all;
                    self.block_all = true;
                    if !was_latched {
                        self.monitor.note_block_all();
                    }
                }
                Scope::Connection => {}
            }
        }

    fn drain_to_upstream(&mut self, index: usize) -> (usize, bool) {
        let secs = self.storage.cache_secs(Instant::now());
        let mut written = 0;
        let mut failed = false;
        loop {
            if self.visit_exhausted(index) {
                break;
            }
            let room = self.io_room(index, usize::MAX);
            let outcome = {
                let ws = &mut self.slots[index];
                if ws.fwd >= ws.buf_len {
                    WriteOutcome::None
                } else {
                    let end = ws.buf_len.min(ws.fwd.saturating_add(room));
                    match ws.upstream.as_mut() {
                        Some(up) => match up.write(&ws.buf[ws.fwd..end]) {
                            Ok(n) => {
                                ws.fwd += n;
                                if ws.gate.is_open() {
                                    ws.arm_idle(Instant::now());
                                }
                                WriteOutcome::Wrote(n)

Per-visit I/O is bounded — src/runtime/reactor.rs:2046-2058

A live visit caps byte work at 64 KiB, narrowing the pre-decision send.

    /// The byte room left in `index`'s live visit; `default` when the visit is
    /// not live, so a single read/write slice can never push a live visit past
    /// the canonical 64 KiB bound.
    fn io_room(&self, index: usize, default: usize) -> usize {
        if let VisitState::Live { slot, bytes, .. } = self.visit
            && slot == index
        {
            (VISIT_BYTES as usize)
                .saturating_sub(bytes as usize)
                .min(default)
        } else {
            default
        }

Reachability

Requires listener access, an approved CONNECT hostname and port with a current eligible DNS binding and matching valid SNI, a configured JA4 Block Connection or Domain policy, and 16 distinct accepted fingerprints for the same domain ordinal. The 17th distinct fingerprint triggers the block while the initiating tunnel can continue relaying. Operator configuration accepts both connection and fqdn JA4 Block scopes; the assigned trace confirms future-CONNECT blocking does not repair the active offender.

  • Attacker: compromised application client with listener access

  • Entry point: CONNECT and initial TLS ClientHello

  • Outcome: continued traffic on the triggering tunnel after the block

Preconditions:

  • Proxy is deployed and reachable by the adversarial workload.
  • An allowlisted domain has JA4 configured to block at connection or domain scope.
  • The per-ordinal baseline contains 16 distinct fingerprints; the next is new.
  • An allowed hostname and current eligible DNS binding exist.
  • The operator configured ja4 block with connection or domain scope.
  • The attacker can send enough distinct valid ClientHello variants to fill the 16-value baseline.
  • Allowlisted FQDN:port and eligible DNS binding
  • JA4 block configured for the allowlist entry
  • 16 distinct accepted JA4 fingerprints previously seeded for that ordinal
  • For Block All, the configured JA4 all-scope gate threshold must be crossed.
  • For pre-decision upstream byte delivery, the upstream socket must already be connected and accept a write before JA4 projection.
  • One allowlisted CONNECT with matching SNI and a usable DNS binding
  • Sixteen distinct JA4 values already recorded for the ordinal
  • A seventeenth valid JA4 value and configured Block action
  • For premature writes, the upstream socket is connected before Hello completion and accepts a write

Existing controls:

  • Exact CONNECT allowlist and matching SNI still apply.
  • All-scope block closes all slots.
  • Domain scope blocks future and other current flows.
  • The CONNECT host and TLS SNI still must match the allowlist; this is a JA4 policy bypass rather than general destination authorization.
  • Exact allowlist pair and SNI/TLS profile check still hold.
  • Block All works; Domain latch blocks future connections.
