    for f in $covered_rs; do
        if [ -L "$f" ] && [ ! -f "$f" ]; then
            echo "INTENDED-COVERAGE-FAIL: .rs symlink does not resolve to a regular file: $f" >&2
            exit 1
        fi
    done
    missing=""
    for f in $covered_rs; do
        case " $INTENDED " in
            *" $f "*) ;;
            *) missing="$missing $f" ;;
        esac
    done
    if [ -n "$missing" ]; then
        echo "INTENDED-COVERAGE-FAIL: physical src/tests .rs absent from INTENDED (drifts outside every identity snapshot):$missing" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    echo "INTENDED-COVERAGE-OK: every physical src/tests .rs (find, untracked included, deleted-indexed excluded) is listed in INTENDED"

  • Attacker: Local actor with checkout write access

  • Entry point: Untracked Cargo build input

  • Sink: E2E source-to-binary identity receipt

Preconditions:

  • Untracked build.rs exists during E2E run
  • Operator treats the receipt as proof of reviewed-source correspondence

Receipt hashes tracked diff and three scripts — scripts/verify.sh:1542-1546

The source input digest has no untracked Cargo build input.

harness2=$(sha256_digest file "$_harness_sh") || exit 1
shellhash=$(sha256_digest file "scripts/verify.sh") || exit 1
printf '%s %s %s %s %s\n' "$head" "$diffhash" "$harness1" "$harness2" "$shellhash"

Source-to-binary claim — scripts/verify.sh:1512-1519

The receipt is intended to establish correspondence with reviewed source.

Severity

Low — This weakens build provenance evidence for an operator using the E2E gates. Exploitation requires an actor who can add an untracked build input in the checkout, and no such actor or file is established in the supplied snapshot. The binary hash still distinguishes artifacts.

Additional runtime or deployment evidence could raise or lower this severity.

Remediation

Reject untracked files before E2E builds or include all Cargo-consumed build inputs in a deterministic source digest. Bind the final receipt to that digest and the executed binary hash.

Summary

Native Rust log and startup test sinks use predictable PID/counter paths and nonexclusive truncating opens. The boot fixture accepts a planted PID/counter directory and writes config.toml through a planted child link. The shutdown E2E script independently truncates fixed /tmp/shutdown-{name}.log paths. The documented host benchmark self-test defaults to shared /tmp: its B8 probe unconditionally truncates /tmp/seam_shell8.out, while TLS branches write fixed certificate and config names such as /tmp/ext.cnf. Each path can modify a runner-writable file if local co-tenancy and filesystem policy permit it; production serving does not call these helpers.

Root Cause

Test and benchmark helpers assume predictable shared temporary paths are private. Rust helpers reuse PID/counter directories or nonexclusively truncate sink files; the host benchmark uses fixed /tmp names, including an unconditional shell redirection. None establishes a private owned namespace and refuses attacker-planted links before writing. The shutdown E2E test also opens a public fixed /tmp log name with wb, without exclusive creation or a private directory.

Both truncating test sink helpers use predictable paths, and the boot helper accepts an existing predictable directory before writing a child config.toml. Each is reachable through the corresponding native tests. Local exploitability depends on shared temporary storage and runner filesystem rights. The shutdown E2E script adds separately reachable fixed-name /tmp log truncation when its cases execute on a shared host.

Assertions:

  • scripts/e2e_shutdown.py:810 and :1252 truncate fixed-name files in /tmp during e2e tests.

Counterevidence and remaining uncertainty:

  • Both affected modules are compiled under cfg(test) (src/log/mod.rs:1041-1042; src/runtime/storage.rs:1672-1675).
  • src/runtime/owner/tests.rs:1116-1134 uses create_new(true), showing a safer sibling pattern.
  • No actual shared test host, higher-privilege runner, or symlink policy was supplied.
  • Only test code uses these helpers.
  • The impact is limited by test-runner filesystem permissions.
  • A private test temp directory prevents cross-user preplanting; Linux protected_symlinks can constrain the direct log-file variant but does not establish ownership of an attacker-created child directory.
  • src/runtime/owner/tests.rs:1116-1134 and src/dns/transport/tests.rs:4994-4999 use create_new(true), which rejects existing paths for those helpers.
  • Per-user temporary directories and isolated containers remove the cross-user preplacement capability.
  • The authoritative benchmark self-test is also documented inside a container, which removes this cross-user host scenario when isolated.
  • Linux sticky-directory protected-symlink settings may block cross-user following; the documented macOS host path and unusual shared-host settings still need their own controls.
  • The production binary does not call these test helpers.
  • Other test sink helpers use create_new(true), which refuses preexisting paths (src/runtime/owner/tests.rs:1116-1133; src/dns/transport/tests.rs:4994-4999).
  • Some Linux shared temporary directories enable protected symlink rules that may block the direct log-file variant.

Limitations:

  • No runtime exploit attempted; host-specific symlink protections and test-runner permissions are unknown.
  • No runtime reproduction or host temp policy verification was performed.
  • No runtime reproduction was performed; actual CI temporary-directory permissions and test runner privilege are unknown.
  • No shared-host runtime proof was performed.
  • Actual CI/local test runner permissions are unknown.

Severity

Low — Local, native-test-only file clobber requires shared writable temporary storage, predictable or raced PID/counter placement, a runner-writable target, and the relevant test execution. Direct sink symlinks also depend on host symlink-following policy; a planted boot fixture directory and child path have a distinct bypass of path ownership.

Private runner temp directories or symlink protections reduce likelihood; a privileged CI runner with shared temp space and predictable test execution raises impact. The benchmark host self-test adds an unconditional fixed /tmp output path; its containerized invocation avoids a cross-user host namespace.

Impact assessment:

  • Level: low
  • Rationale: Conditional integrity loss to runner-writable files; no production proxy network path.

Likelihood assessment:

  • Level: low
  • Rationale: Requires local placement and test timing under permissive host temp policy.

Remediation

Create private, owned, unpredictable temporary directories for native test fixtures, log sinks, shutdown E2E logs, and host benchmark artifacts. Claim files exclusively without following symlinks; reject pre-existing boot fixture directories and child links. Move the shutdown /tmp/shutdown-{name}.log files, unconditional benchmark B8 output, and benchmark TLS certificate/config files under their respective private directories, and clean up only runner-owned resources.

Tests:

  • Precreate a symlink at a candidate temp path and confirm the helper refuses it without changing the target.
  • Run the test suite with concurrent sink creation and verify unique files are created safely.
  • Run tests with a pre-existing symlink and directory at the would-be fixture paths and assert they do not overwrite external files.
  • Preplant a boot fixture directory containing a config.toml symlink and confirm the test helper rejects it without modifying the target.
  • Preplace the expected directory and config.toml symlink, then assert the helper fails without modifying the target.
  • Preplace each log sink filename as a symlink and assert test setup refuses it without truncation.
  • Run the legitimate tests with a private temporary directory and confirm fixture cleanup.
  • Preplace /tmp/ext.cnf as a symlink, run the host self-test with a safe temporary directory, and assert the target is untouched.
  • Preplace /tmp/seam_shell8.out as a symlink and assert the host self-test refuses it without modifying the target.
  • Pre-create the candidate directory with a nested config.toml symlink and assert test setup refuses it without changing the target.
  • Pre-create the direct log-file path or symlink and assert exclusive creation fails without truncation.
  • Pre-create the expected path or a symlink and verify the helper refuses it without modifying the target.
  • Run concurrent test instances to confirm separate private temporary workspaces.
  • Run shutdown E2E cases with a pre-planted fixed-name /tmp log symlink and verify the target is unchanged and the suite uses a private owned workspace.

Preventive controls:

  • Use a shared temporary-resource utility that atomically creates files and directories with private permissions.
  • Use one safe temporary-file helper across tests and avoid predictable PID-only paths.

The relay and shutdown verification selectors certify source-to-binary correspondence using HEAD, git diff HEAD, and hashes of selected harness scripts. An untracked Rust module referenced by tracked source is compiled by Cargo but omitted from this receipt. Its bytes can change during the build or harness without changing the recorded source inputs, so the gate can print a correspondence success for a binary whose full source set was not covered. The documented exact-input receipt omits untracked build inputs even though the binary digest still identifies the executable tested.

The integrity receipt models source as HEAD plus a tracked diff, with manual exceptions for untracked harness scripts, while Cargo may compile other untracked files. The standalone E2E selectors do not invoke the separate untracked-file inventory gate.

# Exact-candidate input digest record (pre/post-build and after the executed
# harness): HEAD + dirty diff + untracked harness py/sh + gate script. The diff
# producer exit is checked SEPARATELY (never a masked pipeline); the untracked
# harness scripts are hashed explicitly (git diff excludes them). Requires $TGT.
e2e_receipt_fields() {
    _gate="$1"
    _harness_py="$2"
    _harness_sh="$3"
    rcd=0
    git diff HEAD >"$TGT/$_gate-diff.$$" 2>&1 || rcd=$?
    [ "$rcd" -eq 0 ] || {
        echo "E2E-$_gate-BLOCKED: git diff HEAD exit $rcd (unreadable diff, not a receipt)" >&2
        exit 1
    }
    rgh=0
    head=$(git rev-parse --verify HEAD 2>&1) || rgh=$?
    [ "$rgh" -eq 0 ] && [ -n "$head" ] || {
        echo "E2E-$_gate-BLOCKED: git rev-parse --verify HEAD exit $rgh (unreadable HEAD, not a receipt)" >&2
        exit 1
    }
    diffhash=$(sha256_digest file "$TGT/$_gate-diff.$$") || exit 1
    harness1=$(sha256_digest file "$_harness_py") || exit 1

Coverage gate would enumerate untracked Rust files — scripts/verify.sh:883-918

An existing gate checks physical src/tests Rust files, including untracked ones, against the intended identity set, but is not part of the e2e selectors.

# F-new (gate-surface-truth M1): the reviewed identity set (INTENDED) must cover
# EVERY physical src/tests .rs file in the current working tree. Physical
# enumeration (find over both roots, all depths, exit captured) includes
# not-yet-staged additions (approved landing could emplace untracked .rs before
# the native-qualified source packet is staged) and excludes already-deleted
# indexed paths (their admission tokens leave INTENDED when the move lands), so
# INTENDED stays the single authoritative admission map while the snapshot set
# tracks reality. A .rs leaf symlink is enumerated, never silently dropped; an
# enumerated symlink that does not resolve to a regular file fails closed, and
# directory symlinks are not traversed. Producer find failure fails closed and
# can never read as a PASS on an empty offender list.
intended_coverage_gate() {
    prc=0
    covered_rs="$(find src tests \( -type f -o -type l \) -name '*.rs' 2>&1)" || prc=$?
    [ "$prc" -eq 0 ] || {
        echo "INTENDED-COVERAGE-FAIL: find exit $prc (tooling error, not PASS)" >&2
        exit 1
    }
    for f in $covered_rs; do
        if [ -L "$f" ] && [ ! -f "$f" ]; then
            echo "INTENDED-COVERAGE-FAIL: .rs symlink does not resolve to a regular file: $f" >&2
            exit 1
        fi
    done
    missing=""
    for f in $covered_rs; do
        case " $INTENDED " in
            *" $f "*) ;;
            *) missing="$missing $f" ;;
        esac
    done
    if [ -n "$missing" ]; then
        echo "INTENDED-COVERAGE-FAIL: physical src/tests .rs absent from INTENDED (drifts outside every identity snapshot):$missing" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    echo "INTENDED-COVERAGE-OK: every physical src/tests .rs (find, untracked included, deleted-indexed excluded) is listed in INTENDED"

Remediation

Hash a complete enumerated compiler source set, including untracked files, before build and after harness; fail if the file list or any file content changes. Run the physical source coverage gate before claiming exact source-to-binary correspondence.

Tests:

  • Reference an untracked Rust module from tracked source, mutate it between receipt checks, and require the e2e gate to refuse certification.
  • Confirm the receipt still accepts a stable source tree and detects changed harness scripts.
  • Run an E2E receipt with an untracked Rust source input and assert that the gate rejects it or records its identity.
  • Change an untracked build input during the build and assert that correspondence verification fails.

Preventive controls:

  • Make source-input inventory automatic rather than manually exempting selected untracked files.
  • Use one shared source-input inventory for all native proof gates.

[30] Two JA4 alerts can lose one triggering peer address

Field Value
Severity low
Confidence high
Confidence rationale Static source shows one overwritten global peer pair, per-ordinal retained fingerprints, and conditional emission based on that pair. No runtime reproduction was run.
Category Deterministic loss of JA4 security-event attribution
CWE CWE-778
Affected lines src/enforcement/monitor.rs:281, src/log/encoding.rs:1014, src/runtime/owner.rs:350

Summary

If JA4 overflows for two allowlisted domains before a monitor report, the monitor preserves both domain fingerprints but overwrites a single global peer address. The report includes the peer address only for the second domain, losing the first alert's destination attribution even when the log sink is healthy.

Root Cause

Monitor::note_fact_ja4_change() stores JA4 values per domain but uses one shared peer IP and ordinal. A later domain overwrites the pair; encode_monitor_domain_batch() suppresses peer output for every other changed domain.

pub(crate) const fn note_fact_ja4_change(
    &mut self,
    ordinal: DomainOrdinal,
    ja4: [u8; 36],
    peer_ip: NumericAddr,
) {
    self.facts.ja4_change[ordinal.get()].bump();
    self.facts.ja4_change_loss[ordinal.get()] = true;
    self.facts.ja4_value[ordinal.get()] = ja4;
    self.facts.ja4_peer_ip = peer_ip;
    self.facts.ja4_peer_ordinal = Some(ordinal);
    self.dirty = true;
}

let ja4_changes = monitor.facts_ja4_change(ordinal);
if ja4_changes > 0 {

    }

Specification binds each reported fingerprint to its triggering peer — docs/alumina-proxy.md:1162-1167

The documented security telemetry contract requires an address aligned with each reported JA4 value.

The C1 latest-change 36-byte JA4 value is keyed per-ordinal, matching the per-ordinal
first-seen JA4 baseline (SP-005, `Ja4BaselineTable`, `src/runtime/reactor.rs` — a 36-byte JA4 per
entry, no per-IP element); there is no per-(ordinal, IP) baseline. The reported value alone
could belong to a different peer than the one whose change fired, so the triggering peer's
source address is carried in the flare/monitor record as a fixed tagged IPv4/IPv6 union,
aligning the reported fingerprint with the change that fired.

Validation

Two domain-specific JA4 changes can be recorded before the owner reports. The second call overwrites the global peer pair, while both domains still have positive counters and retained fingerprints; the encoder omits the first peer field. The specification expects the reported fingerprint and triggering peer to remain aligned.

Validation method: Independent static state and encoding trace

Severity

Low — A reachable client can cause multiple JA4 overflows across domains in one reporting interval and remove a forensic address association from the first alert. Domain identity, counters, fingerprint value, and enforcement actions remain intact; this affects incident detail rather than egress admission. The operator needs at least two allowlisted domains and enough distinct fingerprints for both.

Proof that a deployed collector relies solely on this address for response would raise impact; independent per-event capture or a single domain configuration would reduce it.

Impact assessment:

  • Level: low
  • Why: Loss of one forensic address association impairs triage but leaves action and domain identity intact.

Likelihood assessment:

  • Level: medium
  • Why: A client can vary fingerprints and batch events, but the two-domain overflow setup is substantial.

Remediation

Store the latest triggering peer address alongside each ordinal's JA4 value, or emit a bounded per-event record before another ordinal can overwrite it. Preserve the fixed memory and log-slot bounds.

Tests:

  • Record JA4 changes for two ordinals before one monitor report and assert each emitted d<i>v has its matching d<i>p address.
  • Repeat across report-second boundaries and a healthy sink to ensure attribution does not depend on event order.

Preventive controls:

  • Keep per-domain security-event fields under the same ordinal key when encoding per-domain monitor records.

Field Value
Severity low
Confidence high
Confidence rationale The production enqueue order, queue priority behavior, and in-tree unit assertion directly establish displacement; no live collector was observed.
Category Security event loss
CWE CWE-778
Affected lines src/runtime/owner.rs:30-40, src/log/queue.rs:78-88, src/log/queue.rs:206-227, src/log/tests.rs:1890-1927

Summary

On shutdown, the owner queues shutdown_final as a normal record and then forces a reserved monitor summary before draining. With a full ring, the reserved summary can evict the just-added shutdown_final; an in-tree test confirms the typed status is absent from output.

Root Cause

Terminal logging gives a forced monitor summary priority over a previously queued normal shutdown verdict (src/runtime/owner.rs:30-39; src/log/queue.rs:206-227).

Shutdown record before forced monitor — src/runtime/owner.rs:30-40

The typed verdict is queued as normal before the forced reserved summary.

fn emit_terminal_shutdown_finish(
    storage: &mut ServeStorage,
    sample: (Instant, u64),
    status: crate::log::ShutdownStatus,
) {
    let (now, secs) = sample;
    let dropped = storage.log_dropped();
    storage.logs_mut().shutdown_final(secs, status, dropped);
    storage.report_monitor_if_due(now, true);
    storage.logs_mut().drain_sink();
}

Reserved record evicts newest normal — src/log/queue.rs:206-227

When one slot remains and shutdown_final fills it, the following monitor summary replaces it.

    /// Displaces the newest normal record to admit a reserved one on a full
    /// ring: the reserved block newer than the victim shifts one slot toward
    /// the front and the encoded record takes the newest slot, so only the
    /// newest-lowest-priority record is lost. When every held record is
    /// reserved the newest reserved record is the bounded-not-lossless victim
    /// (docs/alumina-proxy.md:290, :1303).
    fn displace_reserved(&mut self, scratch: &[u8]) {
        let front_started = self.cursor.is_some_and(|cursor| cursor.off > 0);
        let victim = (0..QUEUE_SLOTS)
            .rev()
            .filter(|&j| j != 0 || !front_started)
            .find(|&j| !self.slots[(self.front + j) & QUEUE_MASK].reserved)
            .unwrap_or(QUEUE_SLOTS - 1);
        for j in (victim + 1)..QUEUE_SLOTS {
            self.slots[(self.front + j - 1) & QUEUE_MASK] =
                self.slots[(self.front + j) & QUEUE_MASK];
        }
        self.drop_one();
        let index = (self.front + QUEUE_SLOTS - 1) & QUEUE_MASK;
        self.slots[index].buf[..scratch.len()].copy_from_slice(scratch);
        self.slots[index].bytes = scratch.len();
        self.slots[index].reserved = true;

Validation

Static call trace and the in-tree full-ring test confirm the reserved summary displaces shutdown_final. The shutdown process exit itself still follows the correct typed status.

In-tree test confirms lost verdict — src/log/tests.rs:1899-1927

The test asserts a committed monitor summary and absence of kind=shutdown_final after draining.

        assert_eq!(store.len(), QUEUE_SLOTS - 1, "fill leaves one free slot");

        assert_eq!(
            store.len(),
            QUEUE_SLOTS,
            "the shutdown verdict holds the last free ring slot"
        );
        let dropped_before = store.dropped();
        let mut m = Monitor::new();
        m.note_fact_unknown(UnknownReason::Unattributed);
        assert!(
            store.monitor_summary(101, &mut m),
            "a reserved monitor summary is admitted even on a full ring"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            store.dropped(),
            dropped_before + 1,
            "H2: the admitted summary displaces and counts the newest normal record"
        );
        assert_eq!(store.len(), QUEUE_SLOTS, "the ring stays at capacity");
        flush_all(&mut store);
        let text = String::from_utf8(read_all(&mut file)).unwrap();
        assert!(
            text.contains("kind=monitor"),
            "the reserved monitor summary is emitted: {text}"
        );
        assert!(
            !text.contains("kind=shutdown_final"),
            "the newest normal record (shutdown_final) is the displaced victim: {text}"

  • An external process supervisor may observe exit code independently of stdout.

Limitations:

  • No actual shutdown under a deployed collector was observed.

Client events fill the log ring while stdout is backpressured; later operator shutdown queues shutdown_final; forced reserved monitor summary evicts the newest normal record, including the verdict.

Severity

Impact rises when operators rely solely on stdout for drained-versus-forced shutdown evidence; it falls with independent process-status collection or a healthy sink that drains before the ring fills.

Impact assessment:

  • Level: low
  • Rationale: Telemetry loss only; exit code and tunnel closure still execute.

Likelihood assessment:

  • Level: low
  • Rationale: Requires queue pressure coinciding with shutdown.

Remediation

Reserve priority for shutdown_final and order terminal records so the monitor summary cannot evict it. If both must be retained at capacity, define an explicit priority and displacement policy for terminal records.

  • Repeat with a completely full ring and both drained and forced shutdown statuses.

[32] 32-bit slot tokens stop matching after repeated connections

Field Value
Severity low
Confidence medium
Confidence rationale The 32-bit truncation and comparison are directly evident in source; no 32-bit build or operational deployment was tested.
Category Resource exhaustion / event token truncation
CWE CWE-400
Affected lines src/runtime/reactor.rs:3399-3406, src/runtime/reactor.rs:1462-1477, src/runtime/reactor.rs:1920-1933, src/runtime/tunnel.rs:439-459

Summary

On a 32-bit Linux build, the token holds only 21 generation bits after the 11-bit local ID. Once a slot has been admitted 2^21 times, the encoded generation wraps while the u64 slot generation does not; readiness events are then discarded for that slot. The min-free allocator can repeatedly select that slot for new connections, causing setup timeouts and loss of service under sufficient connection churn.

Root Cause

Slot generation uses u64 storage but event tokens are usize. Packing narrows the generation without wrapping the stored counter to the representable token field, so legitimate readiness can never match once that field overflows on 32-bit.

Generation increments on each admission — src/runtime/reactor.rs:1926-1928

Each accepted connection advances the u64 slot generation.

ws.slot_gen = ws.slot_gen.wrapping_add(1);
ws.capture = SlotCapture::fresh(index, ws.slot_gen);

Allocator selects the lowest free slot — src/runtime/tunnel.rs:458-460

Repeated short connections can concentrate generation increments on the same lowest free slot.

    let min = self.free_heap[0];
    self.free_count -= 1;

Generation is truncated into usize token — src/runtime/reactor.rs:3395-3406

A 32-bit usize has only 21 bits left for generation after GEN_SHIFT=11; bits above that are lost when packing.

fn shifted_generation(generation: u64) -> usize {
    (generation as usize)
        .checked_shl(GEN_SHIFT)
        .unwrap_or(usize::MAX & !LOCAL_MASK)
}

fn client_token(generation: u64, index: usize) -> Token {
    Token(shifted_generation(generation) | (index + 1))
}

Readiness compares truncated generation to u64 — src/runtime/reactor.rs:1462-1477

After 2^21 reuses on 32-bit, decoded event_gen returns zero but live slot_gen is 2^21, so legitimate socket events are discarded.

...

    continue;
}

Severity

Low — This is a high-impact availability failure only on a 32-bit build after about 2.1 million admissions of the same slot. The documented appliance is x86_64, and a supported 32-bit deployment is not shown, making exploitation conditional and low likelihood.

Evidence of a supported 32-bit deployment with sustained connection churn would raise severity; a hard 64-bit compile requirement would make the path inapplicable.

Impact assessment: Sustained connection setup failures on repeatedly selected slot

Likelihood assessment: low

Remediation

Use a generation counter bounded to the token's available bits and compare those same bits, with a wrap-safe stale-event strategy, or enforce a 64-bit build target explicitly. Avoid mixing a full-width stored generation with a truncated token.

Tests:

  • On a 32-bit target or a parameterized narrow-token test, set a slot generation just below 2^21, advance admission twice, and verify current socket readiness is dispatched while stale events remain rejected.

Preventive controls:

  • Add compile-time assertions for token generation width and platform support.

Plain DNS answer redirection candidate DNS origin authentication Rejected Rejected as a vulnerability in the supported bare-IP resolver mode. README.md:51-55 explicitly says plain DNS does not authenticate DNS data; README.md:64-73 makes resolver_trusted the stated default and reserves authenticated assurance for strict-pinned DoT. docs/qa-package/config.example.toml:8,28-29 calls bare IP degraded trust. src/dns/resolver.rs:190-200 selects TCP/53, and src/dns/cache.rs:525 admits that declared profile. No source-backed promise that plaintext answers authenticate hostname-to-IP binding is broken. Endpoint certificate/hostname checking is expressly client-owned (README.md:48-50,86-88). The candidate's on-path redirection dataflow is plausible but within the documented operator-selected limitation.
Plain DNS negative-answer eviction candidate DNS origin authentication Rejected Rejected as a vulnerability under the documented plain-DNS mode. src/dns/wire.rs:1377-1385 accepts NXDOMAIN and src/dns/publication.rs:147-155 evicts both families; this is the intended effect of a resolver negative answer. README.md:51-55 explicitly states plaintext DNS does not authenticate DNS data, README.md:64-73 documents the resolver_trusted default and stronger strict-pinned options, and docs/alumina-proxy.md:51-53 says availability of the egress path is not guaranteed. An on-path adversary can exploit weak resolver transport, but there is no broken authentication or availability invariant promised for that operator-selected mode. Stronger mode blocks this attacker.

JA4 change block on triggering tunnel not recorded Reported Validated JA4 Block enforcement bypass: src/runtime/reactor.rs:2853-2854 can flush ClientHello and coalesced client bytes before JA4 projection when upstream is connected; :2891-2898 ignores effect; project_tripwire :2405-2428 handles only All and Domain, and stop_domain_block :2371-2380 excludes offender. Domain and Connection leave triggering tunnel active, while All can forward bytes before closure. src/enforcement/state.rs:347-366 latches Domain/All but Connection has no runtime closure. docs/alumina-proxy.md:309-311 defines Block scope semantics. Requires an allowlisted host, valid TLS profile and 16 existing distinct JA4 baselines for that ordinal.

Resolver-controlled public address selection not recorded Rejected Rejected as a vulnerability under the repository's stated trust boundary. The default ResolverTrusted requirement intentionally accepts a configured resolver's DNS answer (src/dns/cache.rs:516-529; src/config/mod.rs:944-955). docs/alumina-proxy.md:55 states that the proxy does not authenticate the upstream server; docs/alumina-proxy.md:106-116 states config is trusted and plain TCP DNS is unauthenticated. The proposed attacker already controls the selected resolver or its unauthenticated transport, so supplying an eligible public address is the configured resolver's delegated authority. The proxy still requires exact CONNECT hostname:port, a rooted DNS answer, eligible IP, current cache binding, and matching SNI (src/runtime/tunnel.rs:768-781, 832-847; src/dns/wire.rs:1217-1366; src/inspection/client_hello.rs:874-886). Stronger pinned DoT/DNS assurance are optional operator controls. No source-supported bypass of an active selected assurance minimum was shown.

JA4 action before first upstream write not recorded Reported Validated: hello_complete calls flush_client_upstream before maybe_record_ja4_baseline, and drain may write through buf_len, including coalesced data (src/runtime/reactor.rs:2847-2854, 2931-2937, 2886-2898).
Early upstream activity observation timing not recorded Rejected Rejected. The claimed invariant is stronger than the product's documented observation boundary: docs/alumina-proxy.md:72 explicitly says not to infer arrival ordering for activity first observed after the gate opens; :280 says not to reject fast responses first observed after opening; :303 defines early upstream data as actual I/O observed before opening. The gate opens on successful write accounting through the ClientHello (src/runtime/gate.rs:217-263; src/runtime/reactor.rs:2989-3006). upstream_readable relays only when it subsequently sees an open gate (src/runtime/reactor.rs:2695-2710); closed-gate observations go to observe_upstream_read. Poll-token ordering alone is not evidence that data was observed before gate opening or that an enforced barrier was bypassed.

Predictable local test log file not recorded Rejected Original lead retained. src/runtime/storage/startup_integration.rs:585-601 and src/log/tests.rs:19-35 create predictable temp files with create/truncate; src/runtime/owner/tests.rs:1119-1134 instead uses create_new. The clobber helpers are cfg(test) only (src/runtime/storage.rs:1675; src/log/mod.rs test module), and the supplied proxy threat model has no lower-trust actor with access to the test runner's temporary directory or privileged QA runner. Open Questions And Follow Up

  • src/runtime/owner/tests.rs and src/runtime/reactor/tests.rs received targeted security review but not full line-by-line review.
  • The actual deployed resolver trust mode, firewall confinement, stdout collector, and upstream certificate verification are external operator controls not established by repository source.
  • Are CASE_FILTER or other QA selectors ever supplied from a lower-trust CI input? No such source exists in the inspected repository (scripts/e2e_shutdown.sh:155; scripts/verify.sh:1720-1722).
    • Follow-up prompt: Trace external CI or operator invocations of e2e_shutdown.sh and determine whether CASE_FILTER can cross a trust boundary.
  • Does any test host share a writable temp directory with a lower-privilege co-tenant, and what symlink-follow protections apply? This changes exploitability of the reported test helper issue.
    • Follow-up prompt: Check test-runner temp directory permissions, ownership, protected_symlinks policy and runner privileges.
  • Does any production deployment provide a different firewall, resolver root-validation policy, or stdout collector from the reference guide? None was supplied.
    • Follow-up prompt: Compare the deployed config, firewall, resolver assurances and log collection with the source-backed reference paths.
  • Does the e2e identity receipt need to account for untracked Rust source? It currently hashes HEAD and tracked diff but not untracked source (scripts/verify.sh:1643-1667).
